```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

Here, I will perform analysis on the single-cell level from RCC IMMUCAN data.

```{r load and combine data, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#Load all necessary libraries
library(scater)
library(batchelor)
library(tidyverse)
library(Rphenograph)
library(bluster)
library(scran)
library(RColorBrewer)
library(foreach)
library(clustree)
library(ComplexHeatmap)
library(viridis)
library(dittoSeq)
library(easyalluvial)
library(caret)
library(mclust)
library(scuttle)
library(cowplot)

sce_1 <- readRDS("~/switchdrive/RCC_project/data/rcc_sce_Batch20200528.rds")
sce_2 <- readRDS("~/switchdrive/RCC_project/data/rcc_sce_Batch20201113.rds")
sce_3 <- readRDS("~/switchdrive/RCC_project/data/rcc_sce_Batch20210304.rds")

# Combine different batches
## Synchronize rowdata
universe <- intersect(rownames(sce_1),rownames(sce_2))
sce_1 <- sce_1[universe,]
sce_2 <- sce_2[universe,]
rownames(sce_3)[which(rownames(sce_3) == "LAG3 / LAG33")] <- "LAG3"
sce_3 <- sce_3[universe,]

rowData(sce_1) -> rowData(sce_2) -> rowData(sce_3)

## Combine objects by columns (adding new columns to colData if unique in any sce object - ideally the same columns should be present)
sce <- combineCols(sce_1,sce_2,sce_3)
assay(sce,"exprs") <- as.matrix(assay(sce,"exprs"))
```

## Dimensionality reduction

First, I will visualize the cells in low-dimensional space. If batch effects seem to be present refer to the batch-correction script [here](00_singlecell_batchcorrection.html) or see below.

```{r tsne-umap, message=FALSE, warning = FALSE}
#Select markers for downstream visualization
rowData(sce)$use_channel <- !grepl("Iridium|Histone",rowData(sce)$Target)

set.seed(22)
sce <- runUMAP(sce, subset_row = rowData(sce)$use_channel,exprs_values = "exprs")

plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = "Indication") #should be GU for RCC
plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = "SampleId") #Patient variability?
plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = "BatchId") #Batch effects?
```
## Optional: Batch correction

If batch/patient specific-effects are present, I can perform batch correction with the `fastMNN`(Mutual nearest neighbors) from the [batchelor](https://bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/html/batchelor.html) package. 

**BE AWARE**: In general, *cell-based* analyses are safe to apply on corrected data (e.g. clustering); indeed, the whole purpose of the correction is to place all cells in the same coordinate space. However, the same cannot be easily said for *gene-based* procedures like DE analyses or marker gene detection. See [here](https://bioconductor.org/books/3.14/OSCA.multisample/using-corrected-values.html#for-between-batch-comparisons) for more information.

```{r batch-corr, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
# Run MNN for sample ID correction
set.seed(22)
mnn.out <- fastMNN(sce, batch = sce$SampleId, d=NA, k=20, assay.type = "exprs",subset.row=rowData(sce)$use_channel) 

#the corrected matrix contains low-dimensional corrected coordinates for all cells, which we will use in "cell-based" downstream analyses.
dim(reducedDim(mnn.out, "corrected"))

reducedDim(sce,"corrected") <- reducedDim(mnn.out, "corrected")

set.seed(22)
sce <- runUMAP(sce, dimred="corrected",name = "UMAP_cor") 

#Compare before and after                        
plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = "SampleId")
plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP_cor", colour_by = "SampleId")

###Save RDS object after MNN
saveRDS(sce, "/Volumes/rcc_volume/RCC/IMMUCAN/rcc_sce_BatchCombined_MNN.rds")
```


# Cell identity assignments

Various strategies for cell type assignment are possible. Here I will test following strategies: 
1. **"Cluster & Interpret"** - A.) Graph-based clustering (Stability testing) -> Marker gene scoring -> Manual annotation B.) Graph-based overclustering -> hierarchical clustering (stability testing) -> Manual annotation of cellular meta-clusters 
2. **ASTIR model** - Probabilistic assignment to *a priori* known cell types 
3. **Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM)** - Clustering-based approach for well defined cell type markers 
4. **Gate & Classify** - Cytomapper-based gating for subset of samples ("Ground truth") -> Train random forest classifier -> Classify new data

## 1. Cluster & Interpret

Here I will use Rphenograph (Jaccard-based weights, Louvain clustering as community detection algorithm) and a scran-like pipeline (rank-based weights, Walktrap clustering) to cluster the cells. 

I will use a range of resolution parameters (k=30,50,100) and compare cluster results and stability using `clustree` and silhouette width/purity estimates using `bluster`.

```{r cluster-sweep and testing, message = FALSE,warning=FALSE}
k=100
set.seed(22)
out <- Rphenograph(reducedDim(sce,"corrected"),
                  k = 100)
clusters_100 <- factor(membership(out[[2]]))
sce$clusters_100 <- clusters_100

plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP", colour_by = "clusters_100")

k=50 
set.seed(22)
out <- Rphenograph(reducedDim(sce,"corrected"),
                   k = 50)
clusters_50 <- factor(membership(out[[2]]))
sce$clusters_50 <- clusters_50

plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP_cor", colour_by = "clusters_50")

k=30 
set.seed(22)
out <- Rphenograph(reducedDim(sce,"corrected"),
                   k = 30)
clusters_30 <- factor(membership(out[[2]]))
sce$clusters_30 <- clusters_30

plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP_cor", colour_by = "clusters_30")

##Save RDS object after clustering
saveRDS(sce, "/Volumes/rcc_volume/RCC/IMMUCAN/rcc_sce_BatchCombined_MNN_Clustered.rds")
```

### Cluster stability testing and comparison

```{r clustree, message = FALSE, warning=FALSE, fig.width=10}
#sce <- readRDS("/Volumes/rcc_volume/RCC/IMMUCAN/rcc_sce_BatchCombined_Clustered.rds")

#Clustree
clustree(sce, prefix = "clusters_", edge_arrow = FALSE)

#Pairwise rand index 
#Agreement between two clustering approaches - ARI > 0.5 = "good" similarity
pairwiseRand(sce$clusters_50,sce$clusters_100, mode = "index")
pairwiseRand(sce$clusters_100,sce$clusters_30, mode = "index")
pairwiseRand(sce$clusters_50,sce$clusters_30, mode = "index")

#By clusters for one method
#1. Silhouette width [-1,1]
#Clusters with large positive silhouette widths are well-separated from other clusters
sil.approx <- approxSilhouette(t(assay(sce, "exprs")), clusters=sce$clusters_100)

sil.data <- as.data.frame(sil.approx)
sil.data$closest <- factor(ifelse(sil.data$width > 0, sce$clusters_100, sil.data$other))
sil.data$cluster <- sce$clusters_100

ggplot(sil.data, aes(x=cluster, y=width, colour=closest)) +
    ggbeeswarm::geom_quasirandom(method="smiley")+
  theme_classic()


#Over different resolution parameters 
clusters <- colnames(colData(sce))[str_detect(colnames(colData(sce)),"clusters_")]
df <- foreach(i = seq_along(clusters),.combine = rbind) %do% {
num_clus <- length(unique(colData(sce)[,clusters[i]]))
sil <- approxSilhouette(t(assay(sce, "exprs")), clusters=colData(sce)[,clusters[i]])
rmsd <- sum(clusterRMSD(t(assay(sce, "exprs")), colData(sce)[,clusters[i]], sum=TRUE), na.rm=TRUE)
type <- ifelse(str_detect(clusters[i], "w"),"rank/walktrap","jaccard/louvain")
data.frame(type = type, num_clus = num_clus,k = as.numeric(str_split(clusters[i],"_",simplify = TRUE)[,2]), sil = mean(sil$width), rmsd = rmsd)  
}

gridExtra::grid.arrange(
  ggplot(df, aes(x=k, y=num_clus,color = type))+ 
  geom_line(lwd = 2)+
  theme_classic(),
ggplot(df, aes(x=k, y=sil,color = type))+ 
  geom_line(lwd = 2)+
  theme_classic(),
ggplot(df, aes(x=k, y=rmsd, color = type))+ 
  geom_line(lwd = 2)+
  theme_classic(),
ncol=3
)
```

### Visualization of cluster marker expression 

`Count Normalization`: For visualization I will perform **A. Min-max(0,1)** normalization on the arcsinh (cofactor = 1) transformed counts. (Other options: Z-scores, Winsoring/Clipping)

```{r anno-cluster, message = F,fig.width=15,fig.height=10}
#Min-Max [0,1] normalization of arcsinh-transformed counts
assay(sce, "min_max") <- assay(sce, "exprs") - rowMins(assay(sce, "exprs"))
assay(sce, "min_max") <- assay(sce, "min_max") / (rowMaxs(assay(sce, "exprs")) - rowMins(assay(sce, "exprs")))

#Heatmap visualization (all cells)
dittoHeatmap(sce, genes = rownames(sce)[rowData(sce)$use_channel],
             assay = "min_max", cluster_cols = F, order.by = "clusters_100" , scale = "none",
             heatmap.colors = viridis(100), annot.by = c("clusters_100","Indication"))

#Aggregrate across cells with the mean (median is also possible)
mean_sce <- aggregateAcrossCells(sce, ids = sce$clusters_100,
                                 statistics = "mean",
                                 use.assay.type = "min_max",
                                 subset.row = rowData(sce)$use_channel)

dittoHeatmap(mean_sce, genes = rownames(mean_sce),
             assay = "min_max", cluster_cols = T, scale = "none",
             heatmap.colors = viridis(100), annot.by = c("clusters_100","Indication"))


###Optional: Custom visualization with Complex Heatmap

#Select marker categories for visualization e.g. cell state, cell type markers etc.
rowData(sce)$marker_cat <- grepl("CD",rowData(sce)$Target,ignore.case = FALSE,fixed = TRUE)

###1. Heatmap body
HM_body <- assay(mean_sce,"min_max")
#Colors heatmap body
#col_main <- colorRamp2(c(0, 0.5, 1), c("#0000FF","#FFFFFF","#FF0000"), space = "RGB")
col_main = viridis(100)

###2. Top annotation
#Colors
col = list(clusters_100 = colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9,"Paired"))(length(unique(mean_sce$clusters_100))), 
           Indication = c("lightgreen")
           )
           
col_list_1 = foreach(i=1:2) %do% {
  color= col[[i]]
  names(color)= sort(unique(colData(mean_sce)[,names(col)[i]]))
  color
}

names(col_list_1) <- c(names(col))

#Create annotation
topanno_MCP = HeatmapAnnotation(Indication = mean_sce$Indication,
                                clusters_100 = mean_sce$ids,
                                ncells = anno_barplot(mean_sce$ncells,border = TRUE,gp=gpar(fill="black")),
                                col = col_list_1)
#Plot heatmap
Heatmap(HM_body,
        col = col_main,
        name= "Min-Max norm",
        cluster_columns = TRUE,
        cluster_rows = TRUE,
        row_split = rowData(mean_sce)$marker_cat,
        row_dend_reorder = TRUE, 
        show_column_dend = FALSE,
        #row_title = c("Other","CD markers"),
        row_title_gp = gpar(fontsize = 12),
        row_title_rot = 0,
        top_annotation = topanno_MCP,
        border = TRUE,
        show_row_names = TRUE,
        show_column_names = FALSE,
        column_title_gp = gpar(fontface = "bold")
        ) %>% 
  draw()
```

## 2. ASTIR model

see [here](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2405471221003355?via%3Dihub) for full publication (Geuenich et al.,2021, Cell Systems).

```{r astir-expo}
#Export arsinh normalized expression matrix as csv
#Add sampleID and batchID as covariate in design matrix

expr_astir <- assay(sce,"exprs") %>% t() %>% as.data.frame() %>% mutate(sample = sce$SampleId)

write.csv(expr_astir, file = "~/Desktop/Coding_related/Astir/expr_astir.csv",row.names = TRUE)
```

`Next: Run Astir in conda-environment.`

```{r astir-ana, message = FALSE,warning=FALSE}
#Import Astir cell type assignments
astir_type <- read_csv("~/Desktop/Coding_related/Astir/cell_types.csv",col_names = c("ID","cell_type"),skip = 1)

sce$astir_type <- astir_type$cell_type

#Mark channels used for cell type assignment 
astir_channel = c("CD45RO","CD45RA","CD3","CD68","CD20","Ecad","CarbonicAnhydrase","SMA","CD38","MPO","CD163")

rowData(sce)$use_astir <- rowData(sce) %>% as.data.frame() %>% mutate(use_astir = ifelse(rownames(sce) %in% astir_channel,TRUE,FALSE)) %>% pull(use_astir)

plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP_cor", 
               colour_by = "astir_type", 
               #shape_by = "Indication",
               by_exprs_values = "exprs")

#Heatmap visualization (all cells)
dittoHeatmap(sce, genes = rownames(sce)[rowData(sce)$use_astir],
             assay = "exprs", cluster_cols = F, order.by = "astir_type" , scale = "none",
             heatmap.colors = viridis(100), annot.by = c("astir_type","clusters_50"))

#Heatmap visualization (aggregated)
mean_sce_astir <- aggregateAcrossCells(sce, ids = sce$astir_type,
                                 statistics = "mean",
                                 use.assay.type = "exprs",
                                 subset.row = rowData(sce)$use_astir)

dittoHeatmap(mean_sce_astir, genes = rownames(mean_sce_astir),
             assay = "exprs", cluster_cols = T, scale = "none",
             heatmap.colors = viridis(100), annot.by = c("astir_type"))
```

Next, I will test astir-based cell type assignments in RCC IMMUcan batches.
"Ground truth" = manually labelled cell types by IMMUCAN

```{r astir-test, message = FALSE,warning=FALSE}
#Test Astir performance
#Generate comparable cell labels
unique(sce$cell_labels)

T_cell = c("cytolytic_CD8","CD8_other","cytolytic_exhausted_CD8","Treg","exhausted_CD8","CD4_other","cytolytic_CD4","PD1_CD4","cytolytic_PD1_CD4") 
B_cell = c("B_cell")
tumor = c("Tumor","Tumor_Ki67")
neutrophil = c("Neutrophil")
macrophage = c("Macrophage")
plasma = c("CD38")
stroma = c("Stroma")
unlabelled = c("unlabelled",NA)

sce$cell_label_simple <- colData(sce) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>%
  transmute(cell_label_simple = ifelse(cell_labels %in% unlabelled,"unlabelled",
                                    ifelse(cell_labels %in% T_cell,"T_cells", 
                                    ifelse(cell_labels %in% B_cell,"B_cells",
                                           ifelse(cell_labels %in% tumor,"Tumor",
                                                  ifelse(cell_labels %in% plasma, "Plasma_cells",
                                                         ifelse(cell_labels %in% macrophage, "Macrophages",
                                                                ifelse(cell_labels %in% stroma,"Stroma",
                                                                       ifelse(cell_labels %in% neutrophil,"Neutrophils", "Unknown/Other")
                                                                              )))))))) 

sce$astir_type <- colData(sce) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>%
  transmute(astir_type = ifelse(astir_type %in% c("Unknown","Other","Epithelial"),"Unknown/Other",astir_type))
 
astir_test <- colData(sce) %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% filter(cell_label_simple != "unlabelled") %>% select("cell_label_simple","astir_type")

alluvial_wide(data = astir_test, 
              max_variables = 6,
              fill_by = 'all_flows',
              col_vector_flow = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))+
  theme_classic(base_size = 12, base_line_size = 0.5)+
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank())

run<-unique(astir_test$astir_type)
astir_senspe <- foreach(i = seq_along(run),.combine = rbind,.errorhandling = "remove") %do% {
sen <- sensitivity(table(!astir_test$astir_type == run[i],!astir_test$cell_label_simple == run[i]), negative = "FALSE")
spe <- specificity(table(astir_test$astir_type == run[i],astir_test$cell_label_simple == run[i]),negative = "FALSE")
data.frame(cell_type = run[i], sen = sen, spe = spe)  
}
astir_senspe

ggplot(astir_senspe %>% filter(cell_type != "Unknown/Other") %>% pivot_longer(cols = c("sen","spe"),names_to = "type"), aes(reorder(cell_type,-value), value, fill = type))+ 
  geom_bar(position = "dodge",stat = "identity",color="black")+
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,1))+
  theme_classic(base_size = 14, base_line_size = 0.5)+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),axis.title.x.bottom = element_blank(),axis.title.y = element_blank())+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Paired")
```

## 3. Gaussian Mixture Models (GMM)
Clustering-based approach for well defined cell type markers (such as CD3 for T cells)

```{r subclustering GMM, message = F}
##Method A: Positive or negative for single markers via GMM
GOI = "CD3"
types = "T_cells"

GMM_GOI <- Mclust(assay(sce, "exprs")[GOI,], G = 2)

plot(GMM_GOI, what = "classification")
plot(GMM_GOI, what = "density")
plot(GMM_GOI, what = "uncertainty")

#Classification with uncertainty of 0
GMM_df <- data.frame(class_GOI = ifelse(GMM_GOI$classification == 2 & GMM_GOI$uncertainty == 0, GOI, "Unknown/Other"))

sce$class_GOI <- GMM_df$class_GOI

plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP_cor", 
               colour_by = "class_GOI", 
               #shape_by = "Indication",
               by_exprs_values = "exprs")

GMM_test <- colData(sce) %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  filter(cell_labels != "unlabelled") %>% 
  select(cell_label_simple,class_GOI)

alluvial_wide(GMM_test, 
              max_variables = 6,
              fill_by = 'all_flows',
              col_vector_flow = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))+
  theme_classic(base_size = 12, base_line_size = 0.5)+
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank())

sen <- sensitivity(table(GMM_test$class_GOI == GOI,GMM_test$cell_label_simple == types),negative = "FALSE", positive = "TRUE")
spe <- specificity(table(GMM_test$class_GOI == GOI,GMM_test$cell_label_simple == types), negative = "FALSE", positive = "TRUE")

GMM_senspe <- data.frame(cell_type = types, sen = sen, spe = spe)  
GMM_senspe

ggplot(GMM_senspe %>% filter(cell_type != "Unknown/Other") %>% pivot_longer(cols = c("sen","spe"),names_to = "type"), aes(reorder(cell_type,-value), value, fill = type))+ 
  geom_bar(position = "dodge",stat = "identity",color="black")+
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,1))+
  theme_classic(base_size = 14, base_line_size = 0.5)+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),axis.title.x.bottom = element_blank(),axis.title.y = element_blank())+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Paired")

##Method B: Positive or negative for multiple markers via GMM
GMM_CD3 <- Mclust(assay(sce, "exprs")["CD3",], G = 2)
GMM_Macro <- Mclust(assay(sce, "exprs")["CD68",], G = 2)
GMM_CAIX <- Mclust(assay(sce, "exprs")["CarbonicAnhydrase",], G = 2)

GMM_df <- data.frame(class_CD3 = ifelse(GMM_CD3$classification == 2 & GMM_CD3$uncertainty == 0, "T_cells", NA),
                     class_Macro = ifelse(GMM_Macro$classification == 2 & GMM_Macro$uncertainty == 0, "Macrophages",NA),
                     class_CAIX = ifelse(GMM_CAIX$classification == 2 & GMM_CAIX$uncertainty == 0, "Tumor", NA))

GMM_df <- GMM_df %>% mutate(class_fil = ifelse(class_CD3 == "T_cells" & is.na(class_Macro) & is.na(class_CAIX),"T_cells",
                                     ifelse(class_Macro == "Macrophages" & is.na(class_CD3) & is.na(class_CAIX),"Macrophages",
                                            ifelse(class_CAIX == "Tumor" & is.na(class_CD3) & is.na(class_Macro),"Tumor","Unknown/Other"))))

GMM_df$class_fil <- GMM_df$class_fil %>% replace_na("Unknown/Other")

sce$GMM_class <- GMM_df$class_fil

plotReducedDim(sce, dimred = "UMAP_cor", 
               colour_by = "GMM_class", 
               #shape_by = "Indication",
               by_exprs_values = "exprs")

#Classification with uncertainty below 0.01
GMM_test <- colData(sce) %>% as.data.frame() %>% 
  filter(cell_labels != "unlabelled") %>% 
  mutate(cell_label_simple = astir_test$cell_label_simple) %>% 
  select(cell_label_simple,GMM_class)

alluvial_wide(GMM_test, 
              max_variables = 6,
              fill_by = 'all_flows',
              col_vector_flow = RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"))+
  theme_classic(base_size = 12, base_line_size = 0.5)+
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(), axis.ticks.y = element_blank(), axis.text.y = element_blank())

run<-unique(GMM_test$GMM_class)
GMM_senspe <- foreach(i = seq_along(run),.combine = rbind,.errorhandling = "remove") %do% {
sen <- sensitivity(table(GMM_test$GMM_class == run[i],GMM_test$cell_label_simple == run[i]))
spe <- specificity(table(GMM_test$GMM_class == run[i],GMM_test$cell_label_simple == run[i]))
data.frame(cell_type = run[i], sen = sen, spe = spe)  
}
GMM_senspe

ggplot(GMM_senspe %>% filter(cell_type != "Unknown/Other") %>% pivot_longer(cols = c("sen","spe"),names_to = "type"), aes(reorder(cell_type,-value), value, fill = type))+ 
  geom_bar(position = "dodge",stat = "identity",color="black")+
  coord_cartesian(ylim=c(0,1))+
  theme_classic(base_size = 14, base_line_size = 0.5)+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),axis.title.x.bottom = element_blank(),axis.title.y = element_blank())+
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1")
```
